title: Rook mate: close the box
objective: Use the king to support a rook mate along the edge.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original synthetic lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original instructional text and synthetic rook-mate position

steps.explanation: The rook keeps Black's king near the edge. Bring White's king closer to help the rook.
steps.detail: The rook needs help. Your king can guard the squares where Black's king might run.

question.prompt: Move the king into place, then finish with the rook.
hints: After ...Kb8, put the rook on d8.

tree.feedback: Kb6 covers a7 and b7 and supports the final mating pattern.

children.feedback: Black moves to b8. Give a rook check along the back rank.
Rd8# is checkmate. The rook checks while White's king covers both escape squares.

question.other_legal_move_text: That may keep winning, but this exercise practises the king-and-rook mating pattern.

takeaway: Use the rook to make a box, bring the king close, and give the final rook check from a safe distance.
